clue.text: Cause persistent annoyance in centre of strip joint

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, so we take the middle of strip

parts.note: the ankle is the joint between leg and foot

explanation.surface: A complaint about something irritating at a seedy strip club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' picks the middle letter R from 'strip'. 'Strip joint' reads as one phrase but splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to keep irritating someone long after the event, a verb meaning nag or fester.

clue.text: Skinny person catches animal beginning to champ fodder

indicators.note: one piece catches, or holds, the others inside it

parts.note: a very thin person is called a rake
an ape is an animal

indicators.note: the beginning of champ is its first letter

explanation.surface: A thin farmhand holds back a beast about to munch its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny person' is the container, not the definition; the definition is the last word, 'fodder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapecake is pressed rapeseed residue fed to cattle, so it is a kind of livestock fodder.

clue.text: Nothing removes refuse ultimately from big river

indicators.note: removes says a letter is taken away from the river's name

parts.note: the Nile is a very large African river

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of refuse

explanation.surface: Picture a clean-up crew dredging rubbish out of a great river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E, the last letter of 'refuse', and 'removes' takes it out of NILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is a common synonym for zero, used especially in sports scores.

clue.text: Turn up top of bureau and search around for car document

indicators.note: the word for search goes around the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to look for something is to search

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: the top of bureau is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone rummages through a desk for vehicle paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the logbook was the vehicle registration document; 'up' works as a reversal because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A logbook is the registration paper for a vehicle in Britain, recording its owner and details.

clue.text: Includes maiden among English supporters

indicators.note: among means set in the midst of the other letters

parts.note: braces are straps that hold up trousers
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman is welcomed into a group of English fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts M among E and BRACES. British braces are what Americans call suspenders.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace something is to take it in as a part, a synonym of include or encompass.

clue.text: Female union member attending new entrant?

definitions.text: Female union member attending new entrant?

parts.words: Female union member attending new entrant?
parts.note: reads like a trade unionist escorting a recruit, but the union is a marriage and the newcomer to it is the bride, who is attended by a married woman

explanation.definitionFit: The chief attendant of a bride, when she is herself married, has this title rather than bridesmaid.

clue.text: Revel upset 25 in Gibraltar

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the word for Gibraltar

parts.note: Gibraltar is often called the Rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: the answer to 25 down, a word meaning poorly

explanation.surface: Partying on the Rock leaves someone feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 25, ILL, is 'upset' to LLI and put 'in' ROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To rollick is to frolic boisterously, so it means to revel noisily.

clue.text: Opposing design, noble queen goes over part of garden

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going over another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
a plot is a patch of ground in a garden

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and his queen stroll across a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterplot is a scheme devised to defeat another plot, so a design set in opposition.

clue.text: Quick parking in squalid surroundings

indicators.note: the word for squalid forms the surroundings, enclosing the other letter

parts.note: seedy means shabby and squalid
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a quick parking space in a run-down part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy is a direct synonym of quick or fast.

clue.text: Right way to behave in politics?

definitions.text: Right way to behave in politics?

parts.words: Right way to behave in politics?
parts.note: looks like a question about proper political conduct, but the Right is the political party of the right, and its way of behaving is cautious and traditional

explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a member of the right-wing party is behaving in a cautious, Tory manner.

clue.text: Gang inside got pally, freely speaking many languages

indicators.note: inside puts one piece within the scrambled letters
freely means the letters move about without fixed order

parts.note: a lot is a group or set of people, as in 'that lot'

explanation.surface: A group of friends becomes chummy while chattering away in many tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got pally' reads as the surface story, but it is the anagram fodder that 'freely' scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyglottal describes someone using several languages, from Greek for many tongues.

clue.text: Habitually employ particular church liturgy

definitions.meaning: a distinctive form of church ritual of one diocese, like the Sarum rite of Salisbury

explanation.definitionFit: Use means to employ regularly, and a use is also a local form of liturgy, such as the Sarum use.

clue.text: Rich police officer promises to pay

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
an IOU, 'I owe you', is a written promise to pay; plural IOUs

explanation.surface: A wealthy policeman signs a stack of debt notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful or abundant, the sense of rich in 'a rich supply'.

clue.text: One rewarded with ring following purchase

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces following come below the first

parts.note: purchase is leverage, and to prize (prise) means to lever
the inner is the ring next to the bull on a target

explanation.surface: Someone receives a ring as a bonus after a shopping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' means grip or leverage here, not buying: PRIZE is the British spelling variant of prise, to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: A prizewinner is someone given an award, so one who has been rewarded.

clue.text: Failed to find glove in dictionary

indicators.note: in puts the glove word inside the dictionary's initials

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a mitt is a mitten or glove

explanation.surface: Someone could not find the word glove when they looked it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted is used for something one failed or neglected to do, as in 'omitted to mention'.

clue.text: New Yorkers' breeches, singularly the glory of the parlour?

definitions.meaning: knee breeches named after the Dutch settlers of New York, pictured by Washington Irving's Diedrich Knickerbocker

definitions.text: singularly the glory of the parlour?
definitions.meaning: in the singular, the first word of a tall layered sundae served in an ice-cream parlour, the knickerbocker glory

explanation.walkthrough: A knickerbocker glory is a tall British ice-cream sundae; 'singularly' says drop the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickerbockers are baggy knee breeches named after Dutch New Yorkers, and one knickerbocker glory is an ice-cream sundae.

clue.text: Plant making most of hand itchy somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some new way
most of the word hand means all but its final letter

explanation.surface: A gardener's hand comes up in an itchy rash after handling a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims HAND to HAN; 'somehow' rearranges HAN plus ITCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyacinth is a fragrant spring-flowering bulb, so a type of plant.

clue.text: Point in journey vividly shown according to location

indicators.note: in places the compass point inside the word for journey

parts.note: to go is to travel or journey
E, east, is a point of the compass
graphically means depicted in vivid detail

explanation.surface: A stage of a trip is described in colourful detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographically means in terms of place or position, so with respect to location.

clue.text: More corpulent tradesman, say, Chesterton saw as wicked

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: a grocer is a shopkeeper, a tradesman

explanation.surface: Chesterton's verse paints a fat shopkeeper as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: G. K. Chesterton's 'Song Against Grocers' begins 'God made the wicked Grocer'; that tail describes the tradesman and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean very fat, so grosser is its comparative, fatter or more corpulent.

clue.text: Former army officer's first to analyse and compare

indicators.note: first says the officer's abbreviation comes before the other word

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, with 's standing for is
late means former, as in 'the late chairman'

explanation.surface: A retired colonel was the first to study and cross-check the reports.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Former army officer' but the charade puts COL first: 'officer's first' means the officer is first.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather and examine material side by side, noting differences.

clue.text: Increase rise for favourites at university

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, like a teacher's pet
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Favoured students get a pay rise while at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to raise or intensify, as in stepping up production.

clue.text: Oil spilt on voyage to African capital

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a trip is a journey or voyage

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tanker spills oil on its way to an African port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means after in an across clue, so the voyage word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya in North Africa.

clue.text: Languages from 2 I encountered in Officers' Training Corps

parts.note: the answer to 2 down, meaning nothing

indicators.note: encountered in says the letter is met within the corps' initials

parts.note: OTC is the abbreviation for the Officers' Training Corps

explanation.surface: Someone met nobody in the cadet corps who spoke foreign tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic is the name for a group of East African languages spoken along the Nile.

clue.text: Arcadian god's hollow in ground

definitions.meaning: the goat-legged Greek god of shepherds, worshipped in Arcadia

explanation.definitionFit: Pan is the Greek god of Arcadia, and a pan is a shallow natural depression in the ground.

clue.text: High-risk investment succeeded embezzlement

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
peculation is the theft of funds in one's care

explanation.surface: A risky punt was followed by the theft of company funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculation is buying assets in hope of profit while accepting a high chance of loss.

clue.text: Dicky's brief identification of Midwest state

definitions.meaning: British informal for weak or poorly, as in a dicky heart
the abbreviation of Illinois, a state in the US Midwest

explanation.definitionFit: Dicky is British slang for unwell, and Ill. is the short form of Illinois.

clue.text: Represents private secretary carrying gold salver

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: PS is the abbreviation for private secretary
or is the heraldic word for gold
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: A secretary brings in a golden serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry, a convention solvers meet often.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent someone in art or words.

clue.text: Toast provides physical well-being

definitions.meaning: the word said when raising a glass to someone
the condition of the body being sound and free of illness

explanation.definitionFit: Health is drunk as a toast ('your health!') and also means bodily soundness.
